photo.title: Cherokee chief standing beside a carved and painted totem pole; wearing red and yellow feathered headdress and sleeves.
Cherokee chief wearing red and yellow feathered headdress and sleeves; Cherokee girl beside him wearing yellow fringed dress, boots and headband with feather.
Cherokee chief, Henry, wearing red and black feathered headdress and sleeves; wearing woven decorative bands around waist and head.

Actors recreate scenes from Cherokee history in the play "Unto these Hills" at the Mountainside Theatre: fight scene in which a non-Indian fights with a Cherokee warrior, a second Cherokee character lies dead on the ground; the two Cherokee characters are played by white actors with painted skin and dark wigs.

Three actors recreate scenes from Cherokee history in the play "Unto these Hills" at the Mountainside Theatre: eagle dance scene where one dancer holds large pair of feathered wings; the Cherokee characters are played by white actors with painted skin and dark wigs.
Cherokee man demonstrating blowgun; wearing red and blue shirt with woven belt, beaded necklace and red headband.

Cherokee lady weaving a basket using different coloured grasses to create patterns; wearing  blue blouse and skirt with a beaded necklace; in the replica 18th Century Indian Village at Oconaluftee, which was re-created as a 'living museum'.
Cherokee chief, Henry, wearing red, yellow and black feathered headdress and sleeves; wearing woven decorative bands around waist, head, wrists and over shoulders.

Two Cherokee women making clay pots; surrounded by completed vessels of various shapes and styles; wearing headscarves and beaded necklaces; in the replica 18th Century Indian Village at Oconaluftee, which was re-created as a 'living museum'..
Two Cherokee women making clay pots; surrounded by completed vessels of various shapes and styles; wearing beaded necklaces, one wearing a red blanket.

Cherokee lady weaving a basket using different coloured grasses to create patterns; wearing black headscarf, blue blouse, floral skirt and beaded necklace; watched by young girl; in the replica 18th Century Indian Village at Oconaluftee, which was re-created as a 'living museum'.

Five actors recreate scenes from Cherokee history in the play "Unto these Hills" at the Mountainside Theatre: man in black and red headdress and long cape, flanked by two young men in red and blue clothing, with two Cherokee characters kneeling before him; the Cherokee characters are played by white actors with painted skin and dark wigs.

White actor wearing wig and body paint to portray a Cherokee character; posing with the large feathered wings from the eagle dance scene from the play "Unto These Hills" at the Mountainside Theatre; the Cherokee Alphabet is reproduced on the postcard.
